one_line_contribution: For a retrieved memory item in a fixed-k agent prompt, the per-item credit you get depends on what fills the emptied slot, and the proposal measures three references on the same ALFWorld (game, seed) units - hole (leave-one-out), backfill (the retriever's next-ranked item, which is what deleting the item from the bank actually realizes under a frozen deterministic retriever) and static exemplar - claiming hole credit over-states the value that pruning realizes by at least 8 net per item and by at least 12 net when two items are pruned.
closest_prior_work: Verified: arxiv:2607.14271 (Local Additive Feature Attribution: A Mathematical Taxonomy and Reporting Checklist, S2, 2026-07-15) already names the reference - what replaces the removed input - as one of five specification choices that determine an attribution, and arxiv:2508.14482 (semantic missingness for path-attribution baselines, S2, 2025-08-20) already argues the reference must be a plausible in-distribution state rather than a hole. The proposal cites both and its conceptual thesis is theirs; the increment is instantiating 'plausible state' as the retriever's next-ranked bank item and tying the reference to a pruning decision in a multi-step agent, which neither paper does. Operationally closest is CUE-R (arxiv:2604.05467, verified on both S2 and HF, cit 2), which does intervention-based per-evidence utility with REMOVE/REPLACE/DUPLICATE - but replaces with distractors, in single-shot RAG, with no refill semantics. Also relevant and uncited: 'True to the Model or True to the Data?' (arxiv:2006.16234, found via my query 2), which is the canonical statement that interventional vs conditional reference distributions give different Shapley values for the same feature, and arxiv:2110.11929, which shows deletion-based attribution metrics are biased relative to leave-one-out because the deleted input is off-distribution. Taken together these blunt the claim that 'which counterfactual is item credit' is a new question: it is a known question, and the proposal contributes a measurement of its magnitude in one environment rather than the question itself.
strongest_objection: The headline (P3) is close to an arithmetic consequence of the mechanism (P1), so the design never independently tests 'which reference predicts realized pruning'. D_H = c_H(1) + [s(B12) - s(H2)], and if each emptied slot recovers g >= +8 from its backfill and additivity roughly holds, D_H ~ g_1 + g_2 lands near +16 by construction. The one genuinely open quantity - whether backfill credits themselves add up, D_B - is explicitly demoted to a non-confirmatory estimand. Compounding this: the direction of P1 is near-certain (adding item 4 to a depleted [2,3] can hardly hurt when the bank is procedure-redundant), so the only open question is magnitude, and the proposal's own nested-k prior says items 4-7 add just +2 to +4 on top of the full set. The most likely outcome is therefore 0 < g_1 < +8, which the pre-registration declares neither confirming nor falsifying; the same wide indeterminate zone sits under P4 (0 to +8) and P5 (-2 to +8, already flagged near-entailed by the automated check). A well-powered design whose modal result decides nothing is not a test. Second objection a reviewer will raise: the entire study is at rank 1, gated at c_H(1) >= +10, yet pruners delete low-value tail items, not the top-ranked one - so the reference gap is measured precisely where no pruning decision is ever made, and the operational framing ('only backfill predicts what pruning realizes') is validated on items nobody prunes.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Re-designate the headline: make backfill additivity (D_B, the TOST against +/-10) and the bank-level realization arm R1 (s(B1) - s(R1)) confirmatory rather than time-permitting leftovers - those are the two claims not already implied by P1, and R1 is the only thing that turns 'backfill is what pruning realizes' from an argument into a measurement. (2) Move the primary slot off rank 1: run the hole/backfill/static contrast at a mid or tail slot (rank 3, or a stratum of items whose hole credit is near zero) where pruning decisions actually occur, and report the reference gap as a function of the item's own credit level. (3) Close the indeterminate zones: state P1/P4/P5 as pre-registered interval claims (e.g. TOST that g_1 is inside or outside [+2,+4], the nested-k prior) instead of a one-sided band at +8 with a falsifier at 0. (4) Add the filler placebo below. (5) Broaden the collision check into the ranking/recommendation and corpus-pruning vocabularies, where 'delete an item and the next candidate is promoted' is routine.
missing_baseline: A token-matched filler arm at the emptied slot: [2,3,X] where X is an irrelevant, wrong-type or shuffled exemplar matched to item 4's token count - the program's own measured `blind1` wrong-type placebo generalizes directly, and Appendix B already makes token- and rate-matched placebos binding. As written, B1 = [2,3,4] carries three exemplars and more tokens than H1 = [2,3], so g_1 confounds 'the retriever's next candidate has content value' with 'any third exemplar, or simply more context, refills the slot'. If the filler recovers as much as the backfill, P1 survives numerically while its stated mechanism (bank redundancy, retriever quality) collapses, and P5's reader-invariance claim becomes uninterpretable. A second cheap arm - backfill drawn from a random bank item of the same type rather than the retriever's rank-4 - would separate retriever quality from slot occupancy at one re-run per unit.
preprint_collision: No verified collision. Ten queries, all answered by the s2cli channel (S2 + HF, both reporting ok); WebSearch was unavailable in this session, so no section text was read. (1) 'counterfactual reference choice removing a retrieved document versus replacing it with the next ranked candidate' --recent: 4 results, nearest CUE-R arxiv:2604.05467; nothing on refill/backfill references. (2) 'baseline value choice in feature attribution affects downstream decision removal versus realistic replacement': 12 results, relevant older work arxiv:2006.16234, arxiv:2110.11929, arxiv:2311.00500 - reference choice as a known specification problem, none in retrieval or agent memory. (3) 'CUE-R intervention-based per-evidence utility remove replace duplicate RAG': CUE-R arxiv:2604.05467, CoRM-RAG arxiv:2605.01302, and arxiv:2608.23252 (The Laws of Context Allocation, 2026-08-24, causal measurement probe for evidence utilization plus submodular context scheduling) - the last is the nearest recent item the proposal's own check missed and should be addressed, though it does not compare references or model pruning realization. (4) 'pruning a document from the corpus re-retrieval replaces it with next ranked document data valuation' --recent: 5 results, all reranking efficiency, nothing relevant. (5) 'Shapley value attribution of retrieved documents sources in RAG': 10 results, none makes the claim. (6) 'confidence gain per document attribution DIG RAG': 8 results, none makes the claim. (7) 'remove and retrain benchmark deletion metric out of distribution retraining ROAR': returned only unlearning papers. (8) 'removing an item from a ranked slate promotes the next candidate counterfactual evaluation of item removal in recommendation': nearest is arxiv:2007.12986 (counterfactual slate evaluation with sequential reward interactions) - adjacent off-policy estimation, not per-item reference choice. (9) 'validating memory pruning decisions in LLM agents against counterfactual re-run leave-one-out ALFWorld' --recent: 11 results, none validates a pruning score against counterfactual re-runs. (10) 'does leave-one-out overestimate the cost of deleting a training example replacement effect' --recent: 4 results, unlearning only. ID verification: I verified arxiv:2604.05467 (S2+HF, 2026-04-07, cit 2), arxiv:2607.14271 (S2, 2026-07-15), arxiv:2508.14482 (S2, 2025-08-20), arxiv:2512.10696 ReMe (S2, cit 55), arxiv:2607.22562 SF-AMS (S2), arxiv:2606.29502 UCOB (S2, cit 9), arxiv:2605.04811 TreeMem (S2), arxiv:2605.01302 and arxiv:2605.27105 (HF). I could NOT verify arxiv:2507.04480 (Shapley source attribution in RAG) or arxiv:2509.12765 (DIG confidence gain) - both returned 'not found on S2 or HF' by direct id lookup and did not surface under two targeted topical queries. That is a real weakness rather than a formality: those two are named in the Related Work as the hole-based foils that the whole contribution is defined against, so two of the four pillars of the novelty argument are currently uncheckable. Judging the proposal's own Preprint Collision Check: it is above the norm for this pipeline - four queries, channels named, IDs given, negative results reported as negative rather than as proof of novelty - but it is narrow in exactly the direction that matters. Its 'home' query covered feature-attribution baselines only; it never searched the vocabularies where 'delete an item and the next candidate is promoted' is standard practice (ranking and slate recommendation, corpus/coreset pruning with re-selection, remove-and-retrain evaluation). An AC will read that as searching the literature that supports the framing and not the literature that would deflate it.
